These are the only three settings that change behaviour: High is enhanced reasoning (the default, strong tool-calling at far fewer reasoning tokens), Max is the deepest, and Off disables thinking entirely. GLM collapses its other documented values internally (xhigh to max, low/medium to high, minimal to off), so exposing them would let someone pick Low and still get full High reasoning.

package.name: zai
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# ZAI, fully declarative.
#
# GLM is OpenAI-COMPATIBLE, which is true of the vendor and was not true of our tool loop until
# 2026-07-28. `toolExchange` had been written against OpenAI's RESPONSES API, and Chat Completions
# differs in two structural ways that no amount of manifest could paper over:
#
#   tool calls arrive as FRAGMENTS, keyed by index, `arguments` concatenated across events
#   there is no chain id, so the entire `messages` array is resent every turn
#
# Both are now executor capabilities (`call.each`/`call.index` and `transcript`), so this package needed
# no vendor-specific code — and neither will the next OpenAI-compatible vendor, which is most of them.

name: zai
displayName: Z.AI
description: GLM models from Z.AI, with MCP tool calling and streaming
version: 2.0.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1782027963/gravity/icons/z.svg

features:
  - Multi-turn GLM agent with MCP tool calling, reasoning and streaming

allowedHosts:
  - api.z.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [sse]

credentials.zaiApiKey.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: zaiApiKey
displayName: Z.AI API
description: API key for Z.AI (GLM models). Get one at https://z.ai
documentationUrl: https://docs.z.ai

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Z.AI API key
  - name: baseUrl
    displayName: Base URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: "Override the API base URL (default: https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4)"

files.api/events.yaml:
# ONE ROW PER OUTPUT CONNECTOR, in interface.yaml order.
#
# NO `match` ON ANY ROW, and that is forced rather than chosen: a Chat Completions chunk carries no
# `type` field, so there is nothing to match on. Every row is offered every event and each one's
# expression returns undefined when the field it wants is absent — the emitter drops undefined, so a
# reasoning-only chunk emits nothing on `chunk` without needing a condition.
#
# THE THROTTLES ARE THE CODE VERSION'S OWN NUMBERS, and they are not interchangeable: reasoning is far
# denser than the answer (especially at effort "max"), and each emit re-renders the connected display
# node. Its comment recorded that a 24-char reasoning threshold flooded downstream re-executions and
# could stall completion — hence 150 there and 24 here.

- emit: progress
  from: tool
  # The tool call LOG, written as each tool returns. `from: tool` because our loop produces this, not
  # the stream — the code version built the same line in its own loop.
  value: "return 'Calling: ' + call.name + '...\\n'"
  accumulate: true

- emit: chunk
  value: "return (((response.choices || [])[0] || {}).delta || {}).content"
  accumulate: true
  throttleChars: 24

- emit: reasoning
  # GLM streams chain-of-thought in `reasoning_content`, a field the Responses API has no equivalent for.
  value: "return (((response.choices || [])[0] || {}).delta || {}).reasoning_content"
  accumulate: true
  throttleChars: 150

- emit: mcpResult
  from: tool
  value: "return { name: call.name, arguments: call.args, result: call.output }"

- emit: text
  from: complete
  # THE SETTLED ANSWER, assembled from what was streamed rather than from a final event: Chat Completions
  # sends no "here is the whole thing" message, so the last accumulated `chunk` IS the answer.
  value: >-
    return (events.filter(e => e.emit === 'chunk').slice(-1)[0] || {}).value || ''
files.api/run.yaml:
# GLM's chat-completions endpoint. NO SDK.
#
# `baseUrl` is an OPTIONAL credential field, so the url falls back where it is built — templated, an
# unset value would produce "/chat/completions" against no host.
#
# THE TRANSCRIPT IS SPREAD INTO `messages`, and that is the whole of Chat Completions continuity: there
# is no previous_response_id to name, so every turn resends the history. The loop maintains it and
# hands it over as `transcript`; the SHAPE of a message stays here, because it is the vendor's.
#
# Empty on turn one, so a run that never calls a tool sends exactly system + user.

- name: generate
  method: POST
  url: "return (credentials.zaiApiKey.baseUrl || 'https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4') + '/chat/completions'"

  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.zaiApiKey.apiKey }}"

  # AN EXPRESSION, not an object, because `messages` has to be assembled: a system message only when
  # there is a system prompt, then the user's input, then the history.
  # BUILT WITH `concat`, NOT `push`. The sandbox has no mutating array methods, so `push` would throw at
  # run time — which the expression guard catches at build time. A system message only exists when there
  # is a system prompt, so it is a zero-or-one-element array concatenated in rather than pushed.
  body: |
    return (() => {
      const thinking = config.reasoningEffort !== 'none';
      const head = config.systemPrompt ? [{ role: 'system', content: config.systemPrompt }] : [];
      const messages = head.concat([{ role: 'user', content: config.prompt }]);
      return {
        model: config.model,
        stream: true,
        max_tokens: config.maxTokens || 65536,
        temperature: config.temperature,
        top_p: config.topP,
        // GLM ignores reasoning_effort unless thinking is explicitly enabled, and the two disagree
        // across GLM versions if only one is sent — so both are always set, transcribed from the
        // code version's comment on exactly this.
        thinking: { type: thinking ? 'enabled' : 'disabled' },
        reasoning_effort: config.reasoningEffort,
        messages: messages.concat(transcript)
      };
    })();

  timeoutMs: 600000

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 520, 522, 524]

  transport: sse
  terminator: "[DONE]"

  # A 200 carrying an error body must not read as success.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error.message || 'GLM request failed'"
files.api/toolExchange.yaml:
# THE CHAT COMPLETIONS TOOL PROTOCOL, described here rather than in the platform — a different vendor
# is a different manifest, not another adapter file in the runtime.
#
# It differs from OpenAI's Responses API in two structural ways, and both needed executor capabilities
# that did not exist before 2026-07-28:
#
#   FRAGMENTS      a tool call arrives across MANY events. GLM sends {"qu then ery":"x"}, so reading
#                  `arguments` off any single event yields unparseable JSON. `each` + `index` merge them
#                  and CONCATENATE arguments.
#   NO CHAIN ID    there is no previous_response_id, so `transcript` carries the history instead.
#
# NO `match`, deliberately: a Chat Completions chunk has no `type` field at all, so every event is
# considered and `when` does the filtering.

# How ONE tool is offered. Note the nested `function` object — Responses API puts name at the top level.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function',
           function: { name: tool.name, description: tool.description, parameters: tool.parameters } }
toolsInto: tools

call:
  when: "return Array.isArray((((response.choices || [])[0] || {}).delta || {}).tool_calls)"
  each: "return (((response.choices || [])[0] || {}).delta || {}).tool_calls || []"
  # Merged by INDEX, not id: the id arrives on the first fragment only, so a later fragment has nothing
  # else to join on. Parallel tool calls are why the vendor sends an index at all.
  index: "return part.index || 0"
  id: "return part.id"
  name: "return (part.function || {}).name"
  arguments: "return (part.function || {}).arguments"

# How ONE result goes back: a `tool` message joined to the call by id.
result: "return { role: 'tool', tool_call_id: call.id, content: call.output }"

transcript:
  # The assistant's own words this turn. With preambles on GLM explains itself before calling a tool,
  # and dropping that would cost the model its reasoning thread on the next turn.
  text: "return (((response.choices || [])[0] || {}).delta || {}).content"
  assistant: >-
    return { role: 'assistant', content: text || null,
             tool_calls: calls.map(c => ({ id: c.id, type: 'function',
                                           function: { name: c.name, arguments: c.arguments } })) }

# Always auto: which tool to reach for is carried by the tool DESCRIPTIONS, never by forcing a choice.
choiceInto: tool_choice
choice: auto

# The dial. 1 answers in a single pass and cannot use a tool at all.
maxTurns: "{{ config.maxTurns }}"
# The SAME call with the SAME arguments three times is stuck. maxTurns does not catch it: a model
# calling many DIFFERENT tools forever is not stuck by that rule.
stuckAfterRepeats: 3
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model, prompt]
  properties:
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: >-
        Z.AI GLM model. GLM-5.2 gives the deepest agentic reasoning and honours all three Reasoning
        Effort settings. GLM-5-Turbo is faster and cheaper with 200K context, but reasoning_effort is
        GLM-5.2+ only, so High and Max behave identically on Turbo.
      enum: [glm-5.2, glm-5-turbo]
      enumNames: ["GLM-5.2 (deepest reasoning)", "GLM-5-Turbo (faster/cheaper)"]
      default: glm-5.2
    agentName:
      type: string
      title: Agent Name
      description: Name for this agent (for logs and traces)
      default: GravityAgent
    maxTurns:
      type: number
      title: Max Turns
      description: Maximum agent loop iterations (tool calls plus responses)
      default: 15
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 50
    reasoningEffort:
      type: string
      title: Reasoning Effort
      description: >-
        Depth of GLM-5.2's chain-of-thought. These are the only three settings that change behaviour:
        High is enhanced reasoning (the default, strong tool-calling at far fewer reasoning tokens), Max
        is the deepest, and Off disables thinking entirely. GLM collapses its other documented values
        internally (xhigh to max, low/medium to high, minimal to off), so exposing them would let
        someone pick Low and still get full High reasoning.
      enum: [high, max, none]
      enumNames:
        - High (enhanced reasoning, default)
        - Max (deepest reasoning, most tokens)
        - Off (no thinking, fastest/cheapest)
      default: high
    maxTokens:
      type: number
      title: Max Output Tokens
      description: >-
        Maximum output tokens. CRITICAL with thinking enabled: reasoning counts against this budget and
        the model only emits a tool call AFTER thinking closes, so set it too low and a long reasoning
        pass is truncated before any tool call — the agent then silently never calls a tool. GLM's model
        card recommends 65536 for agentic use.
      default: 65536
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 131072
    temperature:
      type: number
      title: Temperature
      description: Sampling temperature (GLM-5.2 default 1.0)
      default: 1.0
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 1
    topP:
      type: number
      title: Top P
      description: Nucleus sampling (GLM-5.2 default 0.95)
      default: 0.95
      minimum: 0.01
      maximum: 1
    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: Instructions
      description: Agent instructions. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.markdownGuidelines}}.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Input
      description: The request to answer. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order":
  [model, agentName, maxTurns, reasoningEffort, maxTokens, temperature, topP, systemPrompt, prompt]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes that can be referenced in templates
    required: false

# THE NAMES ARE THE CODE VERSION'S, unchanged. A saved workflow references an output by name, so
# `progress` keeps its name here even though `thinking` would read better — renaming it would silently
# empty whatever it is wired to.
outputs:
  - name: progress
    type: string
    description: Tool call log (emitted in real time)
  - name: chunk
    type: string
    description: Streaming LLM text response (emitted in real time)
  - name: reasoning
    type: string
    description: GLM reasoning/thinking stream (separate output)
  - name: mcpResult
    type: object
    description: MCP tool results
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: Final synthesized response

credentials:
  - name: zaiApiKey
    required: true

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    description: MCP service connector — automatic schema discovery
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: false
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: GLMAgent
# A CallbackNode because it STREAMS: the last call's transport is sse, and a tool exchange runs many
# turns. Both are derived and verified by lint, not taken on trust.
kind: CallbackNode

name: GLM Agent
category: AI
color: "#014f56"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1782027963/gravity/icons/z.svg

description: Multi-turn GLM-5.2 (Z.AI) agent with MCP tool calling, reasoning, and streaming

whenToUse: >-
  Run a multi-turn agent on Z.AI's GLM-5.2 that calls tools, reasons, and streams its answer. Pick it
  specifically when you want the GLM model family — large context, strong coding and agentic
  reasoning. It consumes tools from MCP provider nodes attached via service edges.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # An agent is never cacheable: it calls tools whose answers change, and the same prompt legitimately
  # takes a different path on every run.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# The code version's own fixture. Running it live needs ZAI_API_KEY (the credential is named
# `zaiApiKey`, so the bench looks for ZAI_API_KEY).
#
# WHAT IT CANNOT PROVE: the tool loop. With no MCP provider wired the bridge is absent and the node
# degrades to a single streamed turn, which is the correct degradation and also the only path a bench
# can reach. The fragment reassembly and transcript growth are covered by
# packages/base/tests/manifest-toolloop-chat.test.ts against a real server instead.

testData:
  config:
    model: glm-5.2
    agentName: ResearchAssistant
    maxTurns: 15
    reasoningEffort: high
    maxTokens: 65536
    temperature: 1.0
    topP: 0.95
    systemPrompt: You are a concise research assistant. Answer accurately and format the response in Markdown.
    prompt: Summarize the key trade-offs between server-side and client-side rendering for web apps.
  inputs:
    signal:
      topic: rendering strategies
      notes: User is building a content-heavy marketing site and cares about SEO and load time.
  expect:
    # `chunk` streams, so on the bench it is delivered event by event rather than settling — `text` is
    # the one that has to hold the finished answer.
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string' && output.text.length > 0"
